description: Generate database migrations following naming conventions. Enforces table naming (tbl_), column naming (col_), indices (idx_), and standard columns at creation time.
context: Use when creating any new table, altering schema, or writing migrations
checklist: 1. DETERMINE TABLE AND COLUMNS: Identify the resource and required columns. Refer to .ai/database-schema.md for naming conventions.
2. GENERATE MIGRATION NAME: Use timestamp format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_{kebab-case-description}.sql. Example: 20260602120000_create_tbl_user.sql
3. INCLUDE STANDARD COLUMNS: Every table must have: id (UUID), col_created_at_utc, col_updated_at_utc, col_deleted_at_utc
4. FOLLOW COLUMN NAMING: Prefix all data columns with col_, use snake_case, include units if relevant (col_duration_seconds)
5. APPLY FOREIGN KEY PATTERN: Foreign keys named fk_tbl_child_col_parent_tbl. Example: fk_tbl_order_col_user_id_tbl_user
6. CREATE INDICES: Add idx_ prefixed indices on: PRIMARY KEY, foreign keys, frequently queried columns, timestamps
7. WRITE REVERSIBLE MIGRATION: Every UP statement must have corresponding DOWN statement. Never lose data.
8. VALIDATE NAMING: Run schema_validator.py to check table/column/index naming compliance
9. SCAN AND DISCOVER: Run schema_discovery.py to update schema registry
10. VERIFY NO HARD DELETES: Use soft delete (col_deleted_at_utc), never DROP TABLE in code path
11. REPORT SUCCESS: Confirm migration created, naming validated, indices configured, reversibility verified
